title: Characterization of the ACP-mediated effect on the phenotype neutrophilic granulocytes in combination with Geistlich Mucograft®
summary:
In regenerative medicine, there are promising ways to improve the healing and regeneration of tissue. One such approach is the use of special blood concentrates derived from the patient's own blood, such as platelet-rich fibrin (PRF) or ACP (accelerated cells and proteins).  These blood concentrates contain key components that promote wound healing, including fibrin (a protein that supports blood clotting), platelets (which play a role in the healing process), and certain white blood cells (leukocytes, including so-called PMNs). Additionally, they contain growth factors that support tissue regeneration. These concentrates are obtained by drawing blood from the patient and centrifuging it without adding any additional substances. This process concentrate the relevant components of the blood. The exact composition of the resulting concentrate can be influenced by the intensity of the centrifugation process. This study examines how a specific type of white blood cell (PMNs) reacts to a collagen-based tissue substitute material (Geistlich Mucograft®). Additionally, it aims to determine whether the additional application of ACP can modify the response of these cells in a way that further enhances the healing process.
In this pilot study, aims to determine whether ACP can promote the regeneration of a Mucograft® collagen membrane in patients, as has already been demonstrated in laboratory studies.

interventions.name: Wound cover with Geistlich Mucograft(R) in combination with autologous blood concentrate (= treatment group)
Wound cover with Geistlich Mucograft(R) alone (= control group)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Subjects >/= 18 years in good health
- Basal cell carcinoma (BCC) indication in the head and neck facial area
- Indication for excision and defect coverage by means of collagen membrane
- Subjects capable of consenting and who have agreed to the inclusion and participation in the study
- Patients who are able to follow treatment- and study-related guidelines
Exclusion criteria:
- Defect size after excision exceeds the possibility of defect coverage by means of  collagen membrane
- Allergy to collagen
- Corticosteroid intake
- ongoing or already completed chemotherapy
- ongoing or already completed radiation therapy
- Infectious diseases
- General medical contraindications with regard to blood sampling
- No vulnerable groups/minors
- Pregnant and breastfeeding
